pairs: Machabæus autem, et qui cum eo erant,
But Maccabeus and those who were with him,
even recovered the temple and the city.
aras autem quas alienigenæ per plateas exstruxerant,
Then he demolished the altars, which the foreigners had constructed in the streets,
et de ignitis lapidibus igne concepto sacrificia obtulerunt post biennium,
taking glowing stones from the fire, they began to offer sacrifices again after two years,
and lamps, and the bread of the Presence.
lest they should fall once more into such evils,
if they should at any time sin,
that they might be chastised by him more mildly,
and not be delivered over to barbarians and blasphemous men.
Qua die autem templum ab alienigenis pollutum fuerat,
Then, on the day that the temple had been polluted by the foreigners,
it happened on the same day that the purification was accomplished,
vigesima quinta mensis qui fuit Casleu.
on the twenty-fifth day of the month, which was Kislev.
Et cum lætitia diebus octo egerunt in modum tabernaculorum, recordantes quod ante modicum temporis diem solemnem tabernaculorum in montibus et in speluncis more bestiarum egerant.

And they celebrated for eight days with joy, in the manner of the Feast of Tabernacles, remembering that, a little time before, they had celebrated the solemn days of the Feast of Tabernacles in mountains and caves, in the manner of wild beasts.
they now preferred to carry boughs and green branches and palms,
et palmas præferebant ei qui prosperavit mundari locum suum.
for him who had prospered the cleansing of his place.
And they decreed a common precept and decree,
et decreto universæ genti Judæorum omnibus annis agere dies istos.
that all the people of the Jews should keep those days every year.
held himself to be so at the passing of his life.
Nunc autem de Eupatore Antiochi impii filio quæ gesta sunt narrabimus,
But next we will describe what happened with Eupator, the son of the impious Antiochus,
breviantes mala quæ in bellis gesta sunt.
abridging the evils which happened in the wars.
For when he assumed the kingdom,
constituit super negotia regni Lysiam quemdam,
he appointed, over the affairs of the kingdom, a certain Lysias,
leader of the Phoenician and Syrian military.
justi tenax erga Judæos esse constituit,
decided to be strict in justice toward the Jews,
et præcipue propter iniquitatem quæ facta erat in eos,
especially because of the iniquity that had been done to them,
and to deal with them peacefully.
Sed ob hoc accusatus ab amicis apud Eupatorem,
But, for this reason, he was accused before Eupator by his friends,
and was frequently called a traitor.
eo quod Cyprum creditam sibi a Philometore deseruisset,
For he had deserted Cyprus, which Philometor had entrusted to him.
et ad Antiochum Nobilem translatus etiam ab eo recessisset,
And so, transferring to Antiochus the illustrious, he even withdrew from him.
And he ended his life by poison.
Gorgias autem cum esset dux locorum,
But Gorgias, when he was the leader of the places,
frequently made war against the Jews.
Judæi vero qui tenebant opportunas munitiones,
In truth, the Jews, who held the strategic fortresses,
took in those who were fleeing from Jerusalem,
and they attempted to make war.
Hi vero qui erant cum Machabæo,
In fact, those who were with Maccabeus,
per orationes Dominum rogantes ut esset sibi adjutor,
petitioning the Lord through prayers to be their helper,
made a forceful attack upon the fortresses of the Idumeans.
they obtained the places, killing those they met,
et omnes simul non minus viginti millibus trucidaverunt.
and cutting down in all no less than twenty thousand.
Quidam autem cum confugissent in duas turres valde munitas,
Yet certain ones, when they had fled into two well-fortified towers,
gave all appearance of fighting back.
Machabæus ad eorum expugnationem relicto Simone,
So Maccabeus left behind Simon and Joseph, and likewise Zachaeus,
and those who were with them, to fight against them.
eisque qui cum ipsis erant satis multis, ipse ad eas quæ amplius perurgebant pugnas conversus est.
And since those who were with them were sufficient in number, he turned back to those who attacked more forcefully.
Hi vero qui cum Simone erant,
a quibusdam qui in turribus erant,
were persuaded by money from certain ones who were in the towers.
they allowed certain ones to flee.
Cum autem Machabæo nuntiatum esset quod factum est,
But when what was done had been reported to Maccabeus,
principibus populi congregatis accusavit quod pecunia fratres vendidissent,
gathering together the leaders of the people, he accused those who had sold their brothers for money,
Therefore, he executed these who had acted as traitors,
and he quickly captured the two towers.
Armis autem ac manibus omnia prospere agendo in duabus munitionibus plus quam viginti millia peremit.
And so, having success in arms and in all things that he took in hand, he destroyed more than twenty thousand in the two fortresses.
qui prius a Judæis fuerat superatus,
who had been overcome by the Jews before,
calling together a multitude of foreign troops
arrived as if he would capture Judea with arms.
Machabæus autem et qui cum ipso erant,
and those who were with him,
sprinkling dirt on their heads and wrapping their waists with haircloth.
And lying prostrate at the pedestal of the altar,
they beseeched him to be forgiving to them,
but to be an enemy to their enemies,
and an adversary to their adversaries,
they proceeded further from the city, and,
reaching close proximity to the enemies,
Primo autem solis ortu utrique commiserunt:
But, as soon as the sun rose, both sides joined battle:
isti quidem victoriæ et prosperitatis sponsorem cum virtute Dominum habentes:
these ones having the guarantee of victory and success by the strength of the Lord,
illi autem ducem belli animum habebant.
yet the others having courage as their leader in battle.
But, while they were fighting vehemently,
apparuerunt adversariis de cælo viri quinque in equis, frenis aureis decori,
to the adversaries there appeared from heaven five men on horses, which were adorned with bridles of gold,
ex quibus duo Machabæum medium habentes,
having Maccabeus in the middle and surrounding him with their weapons,
being both confused with blindness and filled with disturbances.
Interfecti sunt autem viginti millia quingenti,
Moreover, there were slain twenty thousand five hundred,
Timotheus vero confugit in Gazaram præsidium munitum,
In fact, Timothy fled away to Gazara, to a fortified stronghold,
and those who were with him,
joyfully besieged the stronghold for four days.
trusting to the strength of the place,
But when the fifth day began to dawn,
viginti juvenes ex his qui cum Machabæo erant,
twenty youths of those who were with Maccabeus,
inflamed in soul because of the blasphemy,
manfully approached to the wall, and,
advancing with fierce courage, ascended it.
others also getting up after them,
went to set fire to the towers and the gates,
and to burn the blasphemers alive.
Per continuum autem biduum præsidio vastato,
Then, having continued throughout two days to lay waste to the fortress,
Timotheum occultantem se in quodam repertum loco peremerunt:
they killed Timothy, who was found hiding himself in a certain place.
et fratrem illius Chæream et Apollophanem occiderunt.
And they also killed his brother Chaereas, and Apollophanes.
in hymnis et confessionibus benedicebant Dominum,
they blessed the Lord with hymns and confessions,
qui magna fecit in Israël, et victoriam dedit illis.
who had done great things in Israel and had given them the victory.
